rules: Candidate applicability gate for windbreaks/shelterbelts only. Castle Table 2 PDF p8 places windbreaks on delineated cropland/pasture field boundaries in the US Midwest. WorldCover cropland requires independently mapped field-boundary placement; grassland additionally requires managed pasture confirmation. No universal buffer width or contour-siting rule is inferred. Report applicability zones and candidate line length, never eligible pixel area as planting footprint. Source and cross-context mapping remain pending review. Pete Steward approved B1 on 2026-10-20: boundary geometry required; buffer width varies by publications and regions. Field delineation may be less available in African extensive systems; missing geometry remains unknown. Pete input review 2026-10-20: field boundaries required for both cropland and pasture; no separate pasture-management gate.
status: Configured; requires aligned inputs
dataset_choice_note: No global BIND override; recipe dataset retained
dataset_limitations: Mixed-pixel confusion in fragmented agricultural landscapes. Annual snapshot — does not capture seasonal cultivation. Accuracy lower in arid landscapes and under cloud cover. Not for: Crop-type mapping; sub-field land use classification
weight_note: Configured runtime weight; source-relative importance is reported separately
source_citations: Castle, Sarah; Miller, Daniel C.; Wardropper, Chloe B. (2025). Mapping the social-ecological suitability of agroforestry in the US Midwest. Environmental Research Letters.

label: Land cover / land use class
rules: Pete Steward approved P1 on 2026-10-20: shade agroforestry requires a suitable host crop; OR across crops. Prefer accurate commodity distributions; crop fraction per pixel from MapSPAM is acceptable for high-level scoping. Positive crop fraction establishes host presence, not suitability strength. Retain fractions; no full-pixel area or unverified overlap sum. Source evidence identifies coffee/cocoa systems, not a numeric suitability threshold. No niche-model substitution.
